hints: Exponentiate, rearrange the resulting linear equation in $y$, then multiply numerator and denominator by $e^{-x}$ to reach the requested form.
walkthrough:
Combine the two logarithmic terms using the quotient property $\ln A - \ln B = \ln\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)$:
$$x = \ln(1 - y) - \ln y = \ln\left(\dfrac{1 - y}{y}\right)$$

Exponentiate both sides of the equation with base $e$:
$$e^x = \dfrac{1 - y}{y}$$

Clear the fraction by multiplying both sides by $y$ (given $0 < y < 1$):
$$y e^x = 1 - y$$

Collect all terms involving $y$ on the left-hand side:
$$y e^x + y = 1$$
$$y(e^x + 1) = 1$$

Multiply the numerator and the denominator by $e^{-x}$:
$$y = \dfrac{1 \cdot e^{-x}}{(e^x + 1)e^{-x}} = \dfrac{e^{-x}}{e^x e^{-x} + e^{-x}} = \dfrac{e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-x}}$$

hints: Insert the expression for $y$ from part (i) into the integral over $0\le x\le1$.
Recognise $e^{-x}/(1+e^{-x})$ as the derivative pattern for $-\ln(1+e^{-x})$.
Evaluate at $x=0$ and $x=1$, then combine the logarithms into the stated single logarithm.
walkthrough:
Substitute the expression for $y$ derived in part (i) into the definite integral:
$$\int_0^1 y\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_0^1 \dfrac{e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-x}}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Identify the integrand as matching the standard derivative form $\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$:
Let $f(x) = 1 + e^{-x}$. Then $f'(x) = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(1 + e^{-x}) = -e^{-x}$.
Thus, rewrite the integrand with a compensating negative sign:
$$\dfrac{e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-x}} = -\dfrac{-e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-x}} = -\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$$

Integrate to obtain the antiderivative:
$$\int \dfrac{e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-x}}\,\mathrm{d}x = -\ln(1 + e^{-x})$$

Apply the limits of integration from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$:
$$\Big[-\ln(1 + e^{-x})\Big]_0^1 = \big(-\ln(1 + e^{-1})\big) - \big(-\ln(1 + e^{-0})\big)$$
$$= -\ln(1 + e^{-1}) + \ln(1 + 1) = \ln 2 - \ln(1 + e^{-1})$$

Express $1 + e^{-1}$ as a single fraction:
$$1 + e^{-1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{e} = \dfrac{e + 1}{e}$$

Combine the two logarithmic terms using $\ln A - \ln B = \ln\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)$:
$$\ln 2 - \ln\left(\dfrac{e + 1}{e}\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{2}{\dfrac{e + 1}{e}}\right) = \ln\left(2 \times \dfrac{e}{e + 1}\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{2e}{e + 1}\right)$$
